body:
maya: heads up — we’re getting an alert flood from support: ~20 customers reporting 403s on POST /v1/generate since 09:12 UTC. Dashboard shows spike in auth failures. Looks correlated with the key rotation rollout that started 09:00.

kevin: confirming, I see a surge of 403s and `introspect` errors in auth-service logs. Canary (10% hosts) was green, full rollout started 09:05.

lina: ticket examples: one customer shows `error: token has insufficient scope` on requests that worked yesterday. They’re not calling different endpoints.

maya: tagging @ops-lead — can we pause the rest of the rotation? If rollout is triggering scope mismatches we should stop.

ops-lead: pausing now. I issued an abort to the key-rotator job at 09:17 UTC. Can someone post quick repro steps so support can triage?

kevin: repro we’re seeing: curl introspect against auth-introspect returns 403 for tokens minted before rotation finished. Example: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://auth-internal.prod.introspect/v1``` returns `{ "error": "insufficient_scope" }`. Logs show `token.scope != required_scope` in policy check.

tim: grabbing logs: ```[09:14:33] auth-introspect[worker-3]: token_id=abc123 scope=[read] required=[read,generate] result=fail``` Many tokens are missing `generate` scope even though our token metadata table indicates they should.

maya: hypothesis: rotation process wrote new keys and updated scope matrix, but cache invalidation for token-to-scope mapping missed some shards. Old tokens still hitting services with stale cache state, causing introspect to return outdated scopes.

kevin: digging into cache layer — redis cluster reported a few timeouts around 09:06-09:08 (coincident with the rollout). Could be a race where the rotator updated DB but the cache update failed and fallback to stale entries kicked in.

lina: support noted customers are all across regions (us-west, eu, apac) — not limited to one region.

ops-lead: mitigation plan: 1) pause rotation (done). 2) force cache flush across auth-introspect pods. 3) run a selective backfill to reapply scopes for tokens issued in last 48h. 4) contact affected customers with ETA. Agree?

tim: executing cache flush: ```for pod in $(kubectl -n auth get pods -l app=auth-introspect -o name); do kubectl exec -n auth $pod -- redis-cli FLUSHDB; done``` Running now.

sre-bot: deploybot: cache-flush job started by tim at 09:21 UTC — 6 pods targeted.

kevin: after flush, a few probes look better. Re-running `curl` from earlier now returns 200 and scopes include `generate`. Still some errors for a subset (about 2% of requests).

maya: starting backfill script to reconcile token scopes from canonical DB: ```python backfill_scopes.py --since "2026-03-12T00:00:00Z" --batch-size 5000``` Kicking off at 09:28. Will stream progress.

tim: observed one failure during backfill: DB write conflict on token_metadata shard-7. Retrying with exponential backoff.

kevin: also noticed the rotator rollouts changed the scope-version header key name from `x-scope-version` to `x-scope-v`. Looks like a small config drift in the new rotator image that auth-introspect config expects. Some older pods still reading the old header, causing mismatch.

lina: oh — that header rename would explain why some pods returned old scope sets even after DB was correct. Did canary include both images?

maya: canary used rotator:v2.0.3, full rollout used v2.0.4. v2.0.4 has the header rename — we missed it in the change log. We should treat this as one root cause: header rename + transient redis timeouts -> inconsistent scope read.

ops-lead: rollback option: revert rotator to v2.0.3 to restore header name and re-run backfill. Or patch auth-introspect to accept both headers. Which is faster?

tim: rollback is fastest. Reverting rotator to v2.0.3 for all regions now. Command: ```kubectl -n infra set image deployment/key-rotator key-rotator=registry/redwood/key-rotator:v2.0.3``` Running.

sre-bot: rollout status: key-rotator rollback initiated at 09:35 UTC. 3/6 pods updated.

kevin: backfill progress: ~60% complete, errors retried automatically. Error rate in customer-facing 403s dropped from 18% to <1% after cache flush + partial rollback.

maya: support update sent: "We're seeing transient auth failures tied to a key rotation. We've paused the rollout and are rolling back to the prior safe version. Accept our apologies. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps."

lina: customers reporting improvement in the last 15 minutes. One customer still seeing intermittent 403s; support requested a trace on their failing request.

tim: traced one failing request — it hit auth-introspect pod `introspect-4` which still had old config (didn't pick up rollback image yet) and redis reconnection errors. Pod restarted and now shows new config consistent with v2.0.3.

ops-lead: status check: rotation paused, rollback in progress, cache flush done, backfill 78% and counting. Incident impact: degraded auth for some customers between 09:05-09:40 UTC.

kevin: post-rollback monitoring: 5xxs and 403s stabilized. I'll leave expanded logs on for 2 hours and collect sample traces for RCA.

maya: action items to capture before we close: 1) require compatibility test for header names between rotator and introspect before promoting image. 2) add atomic cache invalidation step in rotator (two-phase commit or publish-subscribe invalidation). 3) improve canary sampling to include a few regions. 4) add a quick rollback runbook for rotator jobs.

ops-lead: agreed. I'll tag this as Sev2 and open followup ticket with owners: kevin (root cause + fix), tim (runbook + cache hardening), maya (customer comms + postmortem).

lina: final note from support: initial estimate ~120 customer requests impacted, majority recovered. We'll send follow-up with affected customers list and support notes.

maya: closing the chat for now — will update once RCA draft is out. Great work everyone. :team_parrot:
